fullText:
Wiz co-founder and CTO Ami Luttwak says AI can now carry out cyberattacks in 20 minutes that once took skilled attackers weeks or months.

In his view, companies need to continuously attack their own systems with the latest AI models to stay secure. For startups, that means building automated testing and patching into the development process from the beginning.

Ami joins a16z's Sarah Wang and Zane Lackey to discuss what changed during Black October, why patching is falling behind, the cost of continuous security testing, and why better security architecture matters more than simply buying more tools.

0:00 Intro

fullText:
Great paper on decision models for long-horizon agents.

For agent RL, you want the decision model to evaluate completed trajectories and leave action selection to the policy.

Decision models output a typed distribution, such as a probability for each option. As actors on ALFWorld, all six models tested (three decision models and three general LLMs) went for an easier subgoal before the one that had to come first.

Shown the full trajectory and asked whether each action helped, the same models gave credit to the steps they skipped while acting.

Used as a teacher for GRPO, one of the decision models raised a Qwen2.5-1.5B policy from 72.8% to 82.9% success on ALFWorld and from 56.8% to 71.4% on WebShop, including on tasks it rarely completes as an actor.

fullText:
Great paper from Google on building benchmarks for data agents.

Static data-agent benchmarks saturate quickly and can't target a specific skill.

SynthCorp generates the data instead. It simulates routine business events and disruptions on a virtual calendar, and those events fill relational tables, a document store, and a data catalog that stay consistent with each other.

Every operation goes into a simulation log, so the gold answer for each task is derived from the log and checked without manual annotation.

The first release has seven data estates with up to 1,000 tables and 256 tasks across five domains. Tasks that chain several business events together still make state-of-the-art agents fail.

一个74M的语音编解码模型：LiquidCodec，让语音AI在CPU上也能高速编解码音频，解码速度达到实时的87倍

这东西对端侧语音Agent、AI眼镜、智能耳机、车载AI来说值得关注

权重已开放，支持本地部署

性能上，在Apple M4 Max、单线程CPU、FP32条件下
音频编码速度达到实时的361倍
音频解码速度达到实时的87倍
同一测试条件下，解码吞吐速度约为Mimi的2.9倍、X-Codec 2的3.3倍

现在大家都在卷语音大模型的理解能力、自然度和实时交互，但还有一个容易被忽视的瓶颈就是音频编解码器

语音模型通常需要先把声音编码成离散的Audio Token，模型理解、推理并生成语音Token后，还要通过解码器把这些Token还原成可以播放的声音

LiquidCodec的技术关键点：

采用GFSQ分组有限标量量化
相比部分传统Codec采用的残差向量量化，它减少了量化码本之间的顺序依赖，让音频Token更适合语音大模型学习和并行预测

优化编解码器架构
采用针对高效计算设计的LFM3架构模块，并优化音频重建过程，减少解码时的计算开销

面向低精度部署
通过量化感知训练，让解码器在Q4_0等低精度条件下，仍能尽量保持声音重建质量，降低模型体积和运行资源需求

更轻量、更快的音频编解码器，可以帮助降低本地语音处理的资源门槛，让实时语音交互更容易在端侧落地

Nice read from Salesforce AI Research and colleagues.

There is a lot of interest in self-improving harnesses, but the harness editor is usually a fixed frontier model.

JoMoHa trains two policies with RL from the same task outcomes. One writes the executable harness, and the other solves the task inside it.

Updating the model and the harness in turns caused trouble. Performance rose and then fell as the two became incompatible. Keeping separate histories and value estimates for each policy fixed that.

JoMoHa beat weight-only and harness-only training on ALFWorld, WebShop, and DBBench, averaging 70.3% and reaching 97.0% on ALFWorld. Training the harness writer also beat freezing it.

// Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement //

Self-improving agents usually keep any harness update that raises the validation score, so noisy gains get accepted, and this later costs performance.

Researchers measured how often this happens. Under a greedy gate, 45.59% of accepted updates were actually worse.

Their gate, TRUST, treats each acceptance as a statistical test and controls the share of accepted updates that cause a real loss. An LLM reads the loop's history to decide how much evidence each update needs.

Across HotpotQA, DROP, and APPS with DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Qwen-3.8-Flash, bad acceptances fell to 2.78%. Final scores were also higher than with earlier statistical gates, which tend to reject good updates.

They prove a bound on bad acceptances and a lower bound on the final gain.

fullText:
The risk with hiring a domain expert for a zero-to-one product is that new products that breakout are always outliers and break the rules.

Foolish people who start from a clean slate and operate from first principles don't have that scar tissue that can cloud decisionmaking. For example, Airbnb had no hoteliers on the founding team.

However, the best scenario seems to be composing the team with both types of people, as it will create the chemistry to avoid obvious mistakes while also questioning "expert" assumptions.
